nonBlockingNotes.note: The first past-ceiling check for any given hang always evaluates PANEHASH-not-yet-written -> prev defaults to literal 'none' -> cur!='none' is true -> CONTINUE once, even for an already-frozen fixer, before a second, later check (with a real prev) can detect the freeze and kill. Additionally, self-fix.sh's own hang-check code (lines 43-61) only re-runs when self-fix.sh itself is re-invoked, and the only unconditional periodic re-invocation is verify-loops-audit.sh's every-6h audit tick (self-fix.sh:37-40's own comment: '...so the 6h audit re-invocation cannot kill an in-progress fix; only a genuinely stuck session (>3h) is replaced, still within the 6h window'). Net effect: a genuine hang crossing the 180min/3h ceiling is detected and killed on the NEXT 6h audit tick after that ceiling is crossed (plus, in the worst case, one extra 6h tick if that next tick happens to be the very first past-ceiling check with prev='none'). This is bounded and eventual -- CLAIM property (d) 'a hang is eventually killed' still holds -- but the effective worst-case bound is closer to ~6-12h than the '180min' name suggests. This behavior and its rationale are already documented in-place in the code's own comments (self-fix.sh:37-40) and were not newly introduced this round (only the boolean's test coverage changed); it is recorded here as a non-blocking clarity note, not a finding, because no CLAIM property is violated and no regression was introduced.
